title: Fuel Cost Calculator: Trip Fuel Cost Estimate
description: Estimate a trip's fuel cost from distance, consumption and price with the Fuel Cost Calculator — dollars or euros, miles or km. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 850 miles at 28 mpg with fuel at $3.60 a gallon burns 30.4 gallons and costs about $109.29 — the trip's fuel bill, known before the trip.
quick_answer: The Fuel Cost Calculator combines a journey's distance with your vehicle's consumption and the fuel price to estimate what the trip's fuel will cost. Enter the three figures — from a route you measured or one you are planning — and read the cost with the fuel quantity behind it.

faq: The price you enter is the price it uses — enter today's local price for a planning estimate. The calculator cannot know tomorrow's forecourt, and does not pretend to.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Traffic changes consumption at the margins; the estimate uses your stated consumption figure, which should be your real-world one.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind. Fuel is burned on road miles — enter the road distance.
Can route results change over time?
Fuel prices change weekly; recompute with the current price when the trip matters.

The structure survives (distance × consumption × price per kWh) — the dedicated EV tools elsewhere on the site frame range; this page is fuel by name and design.
Half the trip was motorway, half hills — one figure?
Use a blended consumption (your car's average over similar mixed driving) or price the two halves as two calculations and add them. The second is fussier and truer.
Should I use the highest price on the route?
For budgeting, yes — planning at the dearest forecourt's price leaves the trip pleasantly under budget everywhere else.
